features.name: Review and change extension settings
entry_points: Settings tab

controls.label: Organization selector
controls.action: Choose or switch the device active organization, apply the active/archived filter, and inspect loading, empty and error states; this view has no clear-selection action.

controls.label: Theme
controls.action: Select system/light/dark and verify applied appearance/reload.

controls.label: Default agent
controls.action: Choose active agent when org is set; inspect empty/unavailable states.

controls.label: Default mode
controls.action: Select Ask/Act.

controls.label: Default speed
controls.action: Select Fast/Thinking.

controls.label: Share page identity & email content
controls.action: Toggle privacy preference.

controls.label: Offer to save logins to Vault
controls.action: Toggle login capture offer.

controls.label: Advanced agent capabilities
controls.action: Expand and operate each capability control.

controls.label: Audit key
controls.action: Inspect public key ID, creation time, receipt count, recent rows, empty state and any actually rendered error feedback; do not infer error handling from source.

controls.label: Collapsible groups
controls.action: Open/close every settings group.

controls.label: Offer saved logins on sign-in forms
controls.action: Toggle saved-login prompt on supported forms.

controls.label: Show password suggestions on websites
controls.action: Toggle password suggestions.

controls.label: Deep clean
controls.action: Toggle deep-clean behavior.

controls.label: Auto-scrape on load
controls.action: Toggle automatic scrape on page load.

controls.label: Desktop bridge pairing
controls.action: Enter pair token and attempt pair; inspect rejection and clear-pair actions.

controls.label: Desktop engine port
controls.action: Edit and save port override; inspect validation and status.

controls.label: Clear local data
controls.action: Open confirmation, cancel, and confirm deletion; inspect resulting local state.

controls.label: Settings sign-in/sign-out
controls.action: Start sign-in as guest or sign out as authenticated user.

controls.label: Required permission: DevTools Protocol
controls.action: Inspect whether the required debugger permission is present; verify its install-time explanation and unavailable guidance. There is no on/off toggle because Chrome does not permit it as an optional permission.

controls.label: Optional permission: Cookies
controls.action: As admin, toggle cookies on and off; verify Chrome grant/removal result, busy state, and reflected current permission. Also deny the grant request.

controls.label: Optional permission: Page archive (MHTML)
controls.action: As admin, toggle pageCapture on and off; verify Chrome grant/removal result, busy state, and reflected current permission. Also deny the grant request.

controls.label: Optional permission: Clipboard read
controls.action: As admin, toggle clipboardRead on and off; verify Chrome grant/removal result, busy state, and reflected current permission. Also deny the grant request.

controls.label: Optional permission: Tab video capture
controls.action: As admin, toggle tabCapture on and off; verify Chrome grant/removal result, busy state, and reflected current permission. Also deny the grant request.

controls.label: Audit key export
controls.action: Export public JWK and verify clipboard result/copy feedback or clipboard error.

controls.label: Audit key re-key confirmation
controls.action: Open Re-key confirmation, cancel and verify key ID is unchanged; reopen and confirm rotation.

controls.label: Audit receipt origin filters
controls.action: Select all, agent, pilot, parallel and webmcp receipt filters.

controls.label: Advanced capabilities member denial
controls.action: Verify guest and ordinary-member Settings omit the admin-only section and do not expose it through any actual Settings navigation.

controls.label: Ask again for a never-capture site
controls.action: Remove one origin from the Never ask list; row appears only after an origin was recorded.

controls.label: Auto-scrape mode: Capture / Scroll & capture
controls.action: Choose and persist either scrape mode.

controls.label: About readiness and installed identity
controls.action: Expand About and inspect detected browser, installed version, extension ID, and saved-login browser support; unavailable support includes an actionable remedy.

controls.label: Check for extension update
controls.action: When browser API exists, request an update check and report available/no-update/throttled/error outcomes; otherwise show browser-managed update instructions.

controls.label: Account identity and role
controls.action: Verify guest email placeholder and signed-in email/name, with the admin badge shown only for admins.

controls.label: Organization archive filter
controls.action: For a signed-in user, select Active, Archived and All; verify available organizations and archived view-only state. Confirm the filter is absent while signed out.

controls.label: Desktop bridge status and health
controls.action: Inspect live connection status and any displayed engine health, version, degraded-service or failed-service details; verify status after the bridge settles.

controls.label: Retry permission status read
controls.action: When Chrome permission status cannot be read, use Retry permission check and verify the error clears or remains truthful.

controls.label: Retry saving preferences
controls.action: After a preference save failure, activate Retry save and verify the latest choice persists without losing newer edits.

controls.label: Retry audit details
controls.action: After an audit details read fails, retry only that read; never rotate a key as part of read recovery.

controls.label: Retry public key export
controls.action: Recover an unsuccessful public-key copy without false copied feedback or private-key exposure.

controls.label: Open Organizations to restore an archived organization
controls.action: Open the configured frontend Organizations page from the archived membership section; navigation does not itself restore or switch organizations.

shared_run_protocol.organization: Record the currently selected device organization for authenticated save. If the UI cannot establish the expected identity or organization, stop that execution as unverified; do not modify organization/account settings to force a pass.
shared_run_protocol.preflight_and_fixture: Before EACH role × lifecycle run, obtain an approved, owner-scoped, read-only exact JSON capture of the target persisted list and compare it with the expanded UI. A UI snapshot cannot see notes or distinguish absent, null, and false optional keys. Mutation is eligible only when that raw list is exactly [] and the UI shows its empty state, with an approved owner-scoped exact-list readback available after writes. Treat this as an empty owned fixture; only same-run synthetic entries may be removed. If the list contains any existing row, is unreadable, disagrees with the UI, or lacks an exact readback path, make no mutation and mark the product row unverified. A separately approved exact capture and restoration method would be required to test a nonempty list; this procedure supplies none. Never clear, delete, reorder, or change existing private rows to create a fixture.
shared_run_protocol.discard_and_back: Before the committed test, create one synthetic unsaved draft change, inspect it, click Discard, and assert the entire target draft list and raw persisted list still equal the empty baseline. Both header and bottom action bars contain Save and Discard; identify which instance was exercised. Click Back and assert the Chat surface is visible; reopen Profile, expand the target section, and confirm the empty list before starting the committed phase.
shared_run_protocol.save_and_reopen: After exercising controls, compare the COMPLETE ordered draft list with expected original [] plus the surviving synthetic entry, including all exposed values and flags. Click a named header or bottom Save and wait for saving to settle. While still in Profile, require no visible profile.error/save error and compare the complete displayed list, then obtain an independent approved owner-scoped raw readback of the entire persisted list. A disabled Save button alone proves nothing. Click Back and assert Chat is visible; reopen Profile and compare the complete list again. For reload dimension, additionally reload the extension, recheck identity/organization, reopen Profile, and compare the complete list and raw readback again. A rejected save or reproducible wrong list is fail; an unreadable/ambiguous write is unverified.
shared_run_protocol.cleanup: Only for an eligible empty owned fixture, remove the surviving same-run synthetic entry through the UI, Save, require no visible save error, and verify both full UI list and approved owner-scoped raw readback equal exact []. Reopen Profile and repeat the UI comparison; repeat after extension reload for reload rows. Never use a blanket clear, direct API/DB delete, or delete any pre-existing row. If a write is ambiguous, stop further mutation until an approved owner-scoped read-only reconciliation establishes exactly what was written; report cleanup_result unverified until empty restoration is proven. If cleanup is attempted and demonstrably fails, report cleanup_result failed. Do not claim cleanup from the UI alone.
shared_run_protocol.failure_semantics: Record product_result pass/fail/unverified and cleanup_result restored/failed/unverified separately for every role × lifecycle row. Reproducibly missing control, save error/rejection, failed Discard or Back assertion, or verified draft/persistence mismatch is product fail, even if cleanup later succeeds. Missing identity/organization, unavailable exact-state capture/readback, uncertain write, or an unexecuted dimension is unverified, never pass. Preserve any product failure alongside cleanup failure. Overall acceptance requires all eight product rows pass and all eight cleanup results restored; any failed row fails acceptance, otherwise any unverified row leaves acceptance unverified. Record safe phase/control identifiers and sanitized error category, never credentials or raw sensitive values.

admin.detail: Verified .90 real trusted Copy all: exact 11 filtered rows of 63 natural rows, Copied feedback and exact 802-byte download; temporary observation permission and prior clipboard restored. cases.title: Verbose console setting
preconditions: Signed in as an admin; open Debug and use controlled non-secret test data.

The selected verbosity governs actual console mirroring: warnings/errors continue in both modes; naturally produced info/success events mirror when verbose is enabled. Setting storage alone is insufficient evidence.

admin.detail: The same natural Bridges Re-discover event was observed on the owned side-panel CDP target with one console match when verbose was on and none when off; setting persistence across real panel reload and restoration also passed. cases.title: Guest cannot open Tasks
preconditions: Use the campaign PLAN.md resource/build receipt. For member/admin choose a device organization and record membership; for guest use a genuinely signed-out profile. Use campaign-owned controlled records.
steps: In guest mode, inspect the tab strip and attempt to navigate to Tasks through any supported tab state restoration path.
expected: Tasks tab is absent and guest cannot render protected task queue.

cases.title: Queue search, project, grouping and sorting
preconditions: Use the campaign PLAN.md resource/build receipt. For member/admin choose a device organization and record membership; for guest use a genuinely signed-out profile. Use campaign-owned controlled records.
steps: As a signed-in member with a selected organization and at least two controlled queue rows, enter a distinctive search term; clear it. Select a project, switch grouping twice, and select another sort option. Reload Tasks.
expected: Search narrows and clear restores matching rows; project/group/sort selections affect visible ordering/grouping and remain consistent after reload.

cases.title: Nested queue filters and reset
preconditions: Use the campaign PLAN.md resource/build receipt. For member/admin choose a device organization and record membership; for guest use a genuinely signed-out profile. Use campaign-owned controlled records.
steps: Open Filters. Select one available domain, status, category, and capture bucket in turn and record row counts; clear all filters. Repeat with an empty facet dataset.
expected: Each selection updates results/count; conditional facets appear only when source data supports them; clear restores unfiltered queue.

cases.title: Row selection and bulk action menu
preconditions: Use the campaign PLAN.md resource/build receipt. For member/admin choose a device organization and record membership; for guest use a genuinely signed-out profile. Use campaign-owned controlled records.
steps: Select one auto-capturable row and one paste-only row. Open bulk resolve and choose each verdict against separate campaign-owned rows; exercise capture with mixed eligibility, then clear selection.
expected: Selection counts match selected rows; bulk capture only processes eligible sources and reports progress; each verdict updates only selected rows; clear removes selection.

cases.title: Single source open, capture, enrich, and verdict
preconditions: Use the campaign PLAN.md resource/build receipt. For member/admin choose a device organization and record membership; for guest use a genuinely signed-out profile. Use campaign-owned controlled records.
steps: Open a controlled source URL and verify it opens separately. Run a normal capture; run a configured enrichment row; exercise awaiting_user Go on a gated fixture. For other rows open Resolve and choose each available verdict, including Retry only after an attempt. Copy URL.
expected: Open acts on the source URL; Run/Enrich starts the matching action; Go resumes user-held capture; each verdict updates that source and Retry visibility follows attempted-level state; copied URL matches row URL.

cases.title: Paste-only source submission
preconditions: Use the campaign PLAN.md resource/build receipt. For member/admin choose a device organization and record membership; for guest use a genuinely signed-out profile. Use campaign-owned controlled records.
steps: Select a paste-only/L4 controlled queue row, enter unique non-secret text in its paste editor, submit, then refresh queue.
expected: Submitted content is acknowledged and associated with that source; refresh shows the resulting status or explicit actionable error.

cases.title: Parallel run session inspection and dismissal
preconditions: Use the campaign PLAN.md resource/build receipt. For member/admin choose a device organization and record membership; for guest use a genuinely signed-out profile. Use campaign-owned controlled records.
steps: Create or observe a controlled parallel run. Expand a sub-run with output, one with an error, and one empty result; collapse and reopen the session; dismiss only after completion.
expected: Expanded rows show URL/output/error/data events as available; empty/running state is explicit; collapse preserves session; unfinished session cannot be mistaken for completed dismissal.

cases.title: Capture, continue, paste, retry, and resolve owned queued sources
preconditions: For each member and admin run, use a separate, real signed-in profile and an explicitly selected device organization. Capture the principal role and organization in the receipt; do not use the active organization as a list filter or infer member access from admin access.

Complete the resource permit and full build receipt required by docs/stabilization/PLAN.md § Build and reload contract. Use the approved receipt-bound extension artifact, verify loaded extension identity and source/tree hashes, reopen the actual side panel, and reload the controlled target pages after any applicable extension reload. Record no secrets.

Use only campaign-owned disposable queued sources in the selected organization, with known URLs and known queue buckets. Prepare separate owned rows for automated capture, user-gated capture, paste, ordinary Retry, and verdict branches, plus a distinct prior-attempt parked row for each policy category (gated_login and low_value), and rows in all six buckets for filter checks. For C18, use an owned source whose URL loads a different page than intended; for C19, use an owned source that is neither dead nor gated. For terminal verdicts, use only sacrificial owned sources with established cleanup ownership. If a required owned row or a naturally qualifying thin response is unavailable, leave that branch unverified; do not repurpose personal/organization records or fabricate backend responses.
Keep one owned ordinary page open in the disposable profile for the source-link check. Do not use an everyday browsing profile. Record fixture identifiers only, not page text or credential data.

Before each capture-level filter check, clear all queue filters, then select only the single tested level; clear it before checking another level. Execution owner must provision and clean up the named disposable sources; until those fixtures exist the procedure is not runnable.
steps: In Tasks, click the toolbar toggle with title 'Group by capture level', then 'Group by project'; confirm the visible queue switches between level sections and project groups. [C20, C21]

Click the toolbar button with title 'Filters'. Under the exact group heading 'Capture level', select each of these six queue bucket options in turn using owned fixture rows: 'L1 · Quick', 'L2 · Scroll', 'L3 · Needs help', 'L4 · Paste', 'Sign-in', and 'Low-value'. For each, confirm only rows in that bucket remain; clear the bucket selection before the next option. If a named option or its qualifying fixture cannot be checked, record that check as unverified. Finish with 'Clear all filters' and confirm the full fixture queue returns. [C22-C28]

For the owned L1 source and then the owned L2 source, click its visible Run/Capture action while its URL is not already the active tab. Observe loading/error/success state and queue refresh. For L2, also observe page settling/scroll behavior on the controlled page. Record the actual terminal UI result; success and thin are distinct outcomes, and an explicit error is not a pass. [C01]

For the owned L3 user-gated source, click Trigger/Capture this tab. Confirm the target page becomes active and the in-page Matrx overlay appears. On this fixture, first click Cancel and confirm the overlay closes while the queued source remains available. On a separate L3 fixture, trigger again, complete the page gate yourself, and click Capture page in the overlay or Go in the side panel; wait for capture submission and inspect the row status. [C02, C04, C11]

On a separate owned L3 source, trigger the overlay and click 'Expect thin content'. If the response is thin, verify the source is resolved as accepted and the page tab is closed; if it is not thin, record that the auto-accept-thin branch was not exercised. Do not induce a thin response by mutating network/backend behavior. [C03]
On the controlled ordinary page, click the queued source URL and confirm it opens that source in a separate browser tab. Return to Tasks. [C12]

For the owned L4 source, enter a short synthetic marker string into the paste field and submit it. Observe success/error and whether the field clears; verify the queue refresh. On another L4 source, leave the field untouched and verify there was no content submission. [C09]

For an ordinary source with a prior capture attempt, open Resolve and verify 'Retry from scratch' is available; select it and observe the verdict response, pending state, and queue refresh. Do not expect this ordinary row to reappear from refresh alone. Repeat Retry on two distinct owned parked sources with prior attempts: one policy_category gated_login and one low_value; observe each pending response and whether its corresponding parked bucket remains visible after refresh. Separately, if an owned capture action produces a real recoverable error, click the row's Run/Trigger action again and observe whether a new attempt starts. If no error occurs, leave retry-after-error coverage unverified. [C05, C13, C17]

Using separate disposable owned sources, open Resolve and exercise the exact labels 'This is the whole page', 'Page is gated', and 'Page is dead / 404'. For 'Wrong content — not what it should be', use a disposable owned source whose URL loaded a different page than intended. For 'Ignore — don't want it', use a separate disposable owned source that is neither dead nor gated. Observe feedback for each verdict; do not choose any terminal verdict for non-disposable records. [C06, C14-C16, C18, C19]

Repeat the applicable warm procedure for each role after the exact extension reload/reopen and controlled-page reload required by PLAN.md. Compare observations independently by role; do not reuse a prior run's result.
expected: Grouping toggles display the queue by capture level or by project according to the selected mode.

The Filters popover opens and exposes the six named capture-level options. Each option filters the rows to its corresponding bucket; clearing the filters restores the full fixture queue. A missing option or qualifying fixture leaves that named check unverified.

L1/L2 actions visibly enter loading phases and either show a successful/thin result followed by queue refresh or a specific recoverable error. Record observed tab behavior without treating unverified backend/parser outcomes as fixed.

L3 Trigger opens the user-gate overlay and waits for an explicit person action. Cancel removes the overlay and clears local in-progress state without submitting capture or removing the queued source. Capture page/Go removes the overlay and submits the currently loaded page; successful thin capture exposes its verdict card, while errors remain visible.

Expect thin content only auto-applies accept_as_is when the returned capture is thin. A non-thin response does not prove the conditional accept branch; unavailable fixture behavior remains unverified. The overlay action attempts to close its tab after capture completes.
The source URL link opens its URL in a separate tab; the Tasks side panel and source row remain available.

Paste submission with non-empty content sends trimmed text for that queued source, shows success or a specific error, and clears the local paste value only after success. Empty content cannot be submitted. Leaving another paste field untouched produces no submission.

Ordinary Resolve → Retry is available only after a prior attempt. Selecting it returns the source to pending and queue refresh reflects the current queue state. An ordinary pending source is not selected by the extension queue, whose ordinary rows require thin/failed status and server_gave_up; therefore refresh alone does not promise immediate reappearance. Expect ordinary-row reappearance only after a separate, actually observed server-processing step changes the source back into a qualifying state. For each distinct prior-attempt parked gated_login and low_value fixture, Retry returns pending; observe whether the corresponding parked bucket continues to include it after refresh under the separate parked-row rule. Do not infer parked behavior from an ordinary fixture. A real capture error remains visible and the row's Run/Trigger action is available for another attempt; absent an actual error, that recovery branch remains unverified.

The current source verdict catalog shows the exact labels 'This is the whole page', 'Wrong content — not what it should be', 'Page is gated', 'Page is dead / 404', 'Ignore — don't want it', and conditional 'Retry from scratch'. Use the different-page fixture for Wrong content and the neither-dead-nor-gated fixture for Ignore. cases.title: Data page identity Retry, failure and recovery
preconditions: Data is visible to guest, member and admin: source registry src/config/sidepanel-visibility.ts:27 sets data to everyone, and src/entrypoints/sidepanel/App.tsx:451-452 renders its tab without an auth conditional. Use a genuine profile for each mode; member/admin org state is recorded but page identity lookup itself is local.

Use the exact fresh unpacked build and record source SHA, dirty-source hash if present, lockfile and output hashes, WXT mode, loaded extension ID, Chrome version, profile/auth/role/org, permissions, backend and fixture. Obtain the stabilization resource permit; after build completion reload the extension when required, reopen the actual side panel on Data, and reload the controlled target tab so its content script matches the build.

Executable fixture is design-needed. The available tests/unit/saved-run-data-view-health.test.tsx DataView route mocks useActiveTab and refreshActiveTabIdentity, and cannot exercise chrome.tabs.query, chrome.webNavigation.getFrame, or a real active-tab switch. Prerequisite: an owned controlled HTTPS test page plus a reviewed native fixture/runner that can cause the first top-frame identity lookup to remain unresolved, then let a later lookup resolve, while recording tab ID and document ID and switching the active tab during a pending lookup. No method for inducing this condition is established by current evidence.
steps: With the controlled page active and its identity unresolved, open Data and record whether the notice displays the current identity error or checking message and Retry. Confirm no page-key-dependent picker or pattern extraction action is available while pageKey is absent.

Click this Data notice’s Retry once. Record the chrome.tabs.query result. If it returns an active tab and this lookup remains current, record the subsequent top-frame chrome.webNavigation.getFrame result; retain only sanitized tab/document identity evidence.

Keep the fixture's lookup unresolved for this attempt. Record the explicit unavailable-identity error, that Retry remains available, and that no field-picker injection or saved/matched pattern extraction starts without a pageKey.

Allow the controlled fixture's subsequent lookup to resolve for the current active tab. Record the returned current tab ID, top-frame document ID and pageKey; verify the notice disappears and page-dependent actions become available only for that identity.

Repeat with an active-tab switch while the lookup is pending. Verify a stale reply for the prior tab/document cannot become the current identity; the resulting identity and any enabled page-dependent actions must correspond to the currently active tab and its document.
expected: Each Retry starts a fresh active-tab query. A top-frame getFrame lookup follows only when the query returns an active tab and the invocation is still current; no-tab or superseded-sequence paths return early. Pending navigation can also return after getFrame. A failed lookup remains explicit in the notice and does not silently produce a page identity.

While pageKey is absent, Data's page-dependent picker and extraction paths stay unavailable; source guards include DataView enterPicker at src/features/data/DataView.tsx:239-240 and handleRun at :343-345.
After a successful lookup, Data uses the current active tab's top-frame document identity and pageKey; the notice is absent only when pageKey is present.

An identity response belonging to a previous lookup or tab cannot authorize page-dependent work on a different current tab/document; record any mismatch as a failure and keep the runtime verdict unverified until actually observed.

expected: Offer from the prior organization is invalidated and cannot be accepted or submitted after the switch.

No credential is written and no website form is submitted during the check.

expected: Replacement process and extension contexts are distinct from the original run.

Vault data is read without creating, editing, or deleting credential records.

cases.title: Summarize and classify active page
preconditions: For cap, selected-label, and invalid-input assertions, use the owned long synthetic fixture. A read-only public page is also valid for a positive summary/classification native acceptance run; record the page identity without copying page text into the run report.
steps: In Tools → Smart tests, expand Summarize active page; set cap to 1k, type to key-points, and length to medium. Run once.

Inspect timing, result or visible refusal, and expand input the model saw. Verify the request event includes the selected type/length and page content is capped at 1,000 characters; use only fixture text.
Expand Classify active page, replace labels with 'article, landing page', and Run. Then enter the invalid one-label value 'article' and Run once more.
expected: The two card headings expand their own controls. Summary selections remain visible and the request event reflects key-points, medium, and the 1k cap; an available API returns a summary, while an unavailable API shows a failure/refusal instead of a fabricated success. Use public page content only for this positive read-only native check; keep cap assertions on the owned controlled fixture.

Classification success returns a label from the submitted set and a confidence value or null. One label produces the visible 'Need at least 2 comma-separated labels.' error and no model-input event for that invalid attempt.
Neither scenario edits or navigates the fixture. Generative wording is not fixed; record the displayed result or exact refusal, not a subjective text-quality verdict.

cases.title: Extract and translate page text
preconditions: Use the owned fixture for marker-schema extraction and malformed-schema negative coverage. A genuinely public page may be used for the read-only translation positive path; record target language and outcome without copying page text into the report.
steps: Expand Extract JSON from active page. Set its schema to {"type":"object","properties":{"marker":{"type":"string"}},"required":["marker"]}; Run and inspect the structured result and model input.
Replace the schema with the malformed text '{' and Run once; then restore the valid schema so the visible control remains usable.
Expand Translate first paragraph, choose German (de), and Run. Inspect the result and model-input panel.
expected: The extraction card exposes the schema editor; valid schema execution displays structured JSON or an explicit runtime refusal. The request event reflects the schema and the fixture is unchanged.
Malformed JSON produces a visible 'Schema is not valid JSON' error without a successful result or model-input event for that attempt.
Translation displays source/target and input/output or an explicit API refusal. Its request events show the source detector followed by translation, and the target is de.

cases.title: Detect, proofread, scan and describe
preconditions: Use the owned controlled fixture for exact typo selection, injection sample, known local PNG, and the no-image sibling. Language detection alone may use a genuinely public page as a read-only positive native check.
steps: Expand Detect page language and Run on the active fixture.
Expand Proofread selection; return to the fixture, select only 'Thiss sentense has a speling mistake.', reopen Tools → Smart tests, and Run.
Activate the owned controlled fixture. Expand Prompt-injection scan and Run on its harmless synthetic PAPERCLIP instruction.

On the owned fixture, expand Describe first image, set the question to What color is the circle?, and Run on the page with the local PNG. Then activate the owned sibling no-image fixture and Run once to exercise the missing-image path.
expected: Language detection shows candidate data or a visible refusal, with scrape/detect timing steps.

Proofread shows the selected input and correction/result or a visible refusal; the page text stays unchanged. With no selected text, the card instead shows the explicit 'Nothing is selected on the active page' error.

Injection scan shows a visible response with suspicious boolean, severity, and reason (plus excerpts when returned); it does not claim a fixed model wording. The captured request contains only the harmless synthetic sample.

Image scenario shows the question, fetched local image preview, and description or visible refusal; the input panel identifies a non-empty PNG Blob. On the no-image page, Run reports 'No images found on the active page.' and no description success.

cases.title: Inspect and copy model inputs
preconditions: Use only owned fixture data and first obtain a successful scenario result. If the API refuses, keep result-copy positive coverage explicitly pending.
steps: After the successful scenario, expand input the model saw and confirm the event count and literal request data are visible.

Click Copy result beside the visible result block and compare clipboard text with that block's displayed body.
expected: Expand/collapse reveals the events emitted by wrapper callbacks in order; fallback requests, if any, appear as separate events.
Copy full payload copies the displayed serialized events. Copy result copies the visible result body exactly.
No copied value contains data outside the fixture. Result copy is only applicable when a result block is rendered; if every scenario refuses, record this positive branch as unverified.

cases.title: Record current tab with and without audio
preconditions: Complete shared artifact/profile setup; sign in as a member or admin with an explicitly selected open organization on this device. Use the owned fixture tab; for the audio-on run, have that tab play only a locally generated test tone after a user gesture.
steps: Open Tools → Recorder. Set Duration (sec) to 1, then 60, and confirm the field accepts both displayed bounds. Set it to 2 for each short capture; toggle Capture audio off for the first and on for the second.

With the fixture active, click Record. If Chrome asks for optional tabCapture permission, grant it for this positive path. Observe Checking permission/Starting/Recording and elapsed time, then click Stop before the duration expires.

Wait for Finalizing/Uploading to finish; inspect the saved row, duration, title, MIME, size, and audio badge. Reload the side panel/extension using the documented artifact cycle and confirm the metadata row rehydrates.
expected: Duration bounds are 1 and 60 seconds; recording uses the clamped seconds value. Controls are disabled during busy states, and Stop is shown while recording.

Successful captures return to Idle after upload and add a local recording row. Audio badge is absent for audio off and present for audio on; the saved metadata survives reload. The actual video bytes are stored as a file; the row is only local metadata.
If capture or upload refuses, the error/recovery UI must be visible; do not mark positive upload or persistence as passed.

cases.title: Recover from permission rejection
preconditions: Use a disposable signed-in profile with active organization but tabCapture not granted. Permission state must be reset between denial variants by removing/readding this exact unpacked artifact and rechecking its Loaded from path and tree hash.
steps: Click Record and decline Chrome's tabCapture request. Confirm the recovery dialog appears only after denial; test X, Close, and backdrop dismissal in separate reset runs. Each dismissal should close the dialog without opening another tab.

cases.title: Controlled manual execution: chrome_batch
preconditions: Before each case, obtain the resource permit required by docs/stabilization/PLAN.md and write a fresh receipt: source SHA and dirty-source hash if applicable, lockfile hash, output hash, WXT mode, extension runtime ID, Chrome version, profile label, auth/role/org state, permissions, backend identity, fixture IDs and timestamp. Also record login method, principal provenance, real data origin, build/env flags, response interception, mocks and seeded browser state. No credentials, tokens, session data or page contents.

Use an already built, receipt-bound unpacked development artifact. Confirm loaded extension ID, source/output identity and build fingerprint. Wait for build completion before reload; reload the extension when required, reopen extension pages and the actual side panel/Tools tab, and reload controlled target tabs after extension reload. Treat service worker and offscreen contexts separately and verify each running build identity before acting. If either required context cannot be independently identified, leave that context/lifecycle dimension unverified and do not proceed as though its build identity is established. HMR alone is not acceptance evidence.

Run separately in genuine signed-in member and admin profiles. Tools is signed-in-only; guest applicability is not added by these proposals. Keep device organization and role visible in the receipt; do not infer one role's behavior from the other. Use only the owned public HTTPS fixtures described below.

Actual UI route: open the extension side panel, select Tools > Catalog, select All handlers, search and expand the exact handler, inspect its displayed local JSON schema, enter the specified JSON in Test runner and press Run. This route is source-confirmed in src/features/tools/ToolsView.tsx. It parses JSON and safe-parses local schemas, then calls handler.run directly with permissionMode=act and assignedTabId=null. It bypasses dispatcher permission/approval and role gates; these procedures do not establish dispatcher behavior, denied-permission behavior or live DB binding/advertisement.

Immediately before each Run, verify the selected active tab in the disposable test Chrome window is the owned public HTTPS fixture. Do not run in an everyday browsing profile. If the actual UI route, receipt or target focus cannot be established, leave the case unverified. Preserve original browser state and close only fixture tabs created by that case.

This source-only proposal covers warm direct-handler runs and the stated extension-reload observations only. Cold/idle service-worker restart with DevTools closed, controlled-page navigation, permission-denied recovery, and offline recovery are explicitly outside this proposal and remain unverified; do not count them as coverage or acceptance. No lifecycle fault may be inferred from these procedures.
Use the shared receipt and reload preamble. Verify current active tab is https://example.com/ in the disposable profile; this case only reads the public page/tab listing.
Use separate genuine member and admin profiles. Do not use private browsing, injected sessions or mocked services. No backend data fixture is needed.
steps: Run {"calls":[{"name":"list_open_tabs","arguments":{"all_windows":false,"url":"https://example.com/*"}}],"stop_on_error":true}. Confirm one ordered result and that the nested output reports the owned example.com fixture tab, without recording other tab URLs or titles.

Run {"calls":[{"name":"missing_test_tool_20261007","arguments":{}},{"name":"list_open_tabs","arguments":{"all_windows":false,"url":"https://example.com/*"}}]}. Confirm unknown-tool failure is itemized and, with default stop_on_error=false, the second read is still returned.

Run {"calls":[{"name":"navigate","arguments":{"url":"https://example.com/"}}],"stop_on_error":true}. Confirm the nested non-read action is rejected before it runs; verify the selected fixture URL did not change.
Run {"calls":[],"stop_on_error":true}. Confirm the manual runner reports a schema mismatch before handler.run.

After full extension reload and reopening Tools, repeat the first read once in the warm/reloaded state. Do not claim service-worker idle-restart or offscreen-recreation coverage unless those contexts were independently observed.
expected: The first call returns count=1, results[0].ok=true, name=list_open_tabs and a nested list containing the owned fixture tab. No navigation, write or other action occurs.
The unknown nested name produces an item-level ok=false with an unknown-tool error; because stop_on_error defaults false, the following list call is also attempted and returned.
The action-tier navigate call returns an item-level ok=false with the source-defined read-tier-only error and does not navigate the fixture tab.
An empty calls array is rejected by the outer schema, so no batch call executes.

Reloaded direct-run behavior is recorded separately. Dispatcher approval/denial, optional permission refusal, registered binding and a real agent-dispatched batch remain unverified by this manual route.

source_anchors: src/lib/tools/handlers/batch.ts:24-94 — nonempty calls array up to 20, lookup, read-tier enforcement, nested schema parsing, per-call result collection and stop_on_error.
src/lib/tools/registry.ts — canonical handler registration and lookup used by chrome_batch.
src/features/tools/ToolsView.tsx:346-462,510-545 — displayed schema, JSON runner, direct handler invocation, visible result/error.
src/lib/tools/dispatch.ts — outer dispatcher permission gate; not exercised by the manual runner.
procedure_source_review.limits: chrome_batch declares no required permissions in types/tool-catalog.md; nested tool permission gates are not run because the handler executes nested read handlers directly. No permission-denied or dispatcher result is inferred. This proposal is not a runtime pass. Cold idle restart, controlled-page navigation, permission-denied recovery and offline recovery are outside this proposal and remain unverified; do not count the extension reload as those dimensions. Verify service-worker and offscreen build identity before an actual run; otherwise stop and leave execution unverified.

preconditions: Follow the full resource/build/reload preflight in docs/stabilization/PLAN.md. Use a current imported development artifact selected from its receipt set, not a directory name. Load the exact receipt-bound chrome-mv3 folder if needed, reload the extension, close/reopen the side panel, then reload the selected target tab. Keep each case unverified until actually run against that artifact.

Use an existing signed-in member profile and repeat in an existing signed-in admin profile; do not change account roles. In Tools, find the named tool, expand its argument form, enter the case JSON, select Run, and inspect the inline result. This is a one-tool, user-initiated local run.

ToolsView.tsx says the manual Run skips the permission gate. Therefore these procedures verify manual handler behavior only; they do not verify dispatcher Ask/Act authorization or prove that a withheld Chrome permission is enforced. Do not remove permissions to manufacture a denial. Any permission refusal observed in normal operation is reportable, but is not a required negative test here.

Use a dedicated disposable Chrome profile containing only public targets and synthetic bookmarks/history for the browser-data cases. Never inspect or report the user's ordinary bookmarks or browsing history. Public page reads are read-only; do not submit forms or copy arbitrary page content into reports.
Complete shared receipt-bound build/profile/reload setup.
Open public https://example.org/ in the active tab and confirm it is fully loaded; use no logged-in or personal page.
Warm/reload repetition: Run once on the warm loaded page; then reload extension, panel, and same target tab and rerun both filter calls.
steps: Warm execution: perform the following tool action(s) once before any case-specific extension/tab reload and record the inline result for comparison.
In Tools, open read_page and run with {"filter":"all","include_text":true,"include_bounds":false,"max_nodes":200}.

Inspect the inline result for the active page title/URL and returned element roles, names/text, and refs. Confirm the visible heading text appears; do not enable lazy-load or hidden-element collection for this baseline.
Run again with {"filter":"interactive","include_text":true,"max_nodes":200} and compare the returned elements.

After this warm pass, reload the extension, close/reopen Tools, and reload the same public tab. Repeat both read_page calls and apply the same heading/filter checks; compare visible content rather than refs.
expected: The all-elements result includes visible page content and element metadata, including the public heading; the interactive result contains only interactive elements. Visible page text and navigation remain unchanged. read_page clears/reapplies data-matrx-ref attributes in the DOM, so this is a visible-content-preserving read with a DOM metadata side effect.
If the tab is unsupported or scripting access is unavailable, the tool returns a visible refusal/error; do not count an empty/error result as a successful content read.
procedure_limits: Exact node count and refs can vary with page/browser rendering; assert visible heading and role/filter behavior, not a fixed whole-page scrape.
The handler removes stale data-matrx-ref attributes and stamps current refs; do not describe the call as causing zero DOM mutation.
Inventory says guest is not applicable because Tools requires sign-in. Member/admin are applicable. Manual Run bypasses dispatcher authorization; this case does not cover Ask/Act.

steps: Warm execution: perform this sequence once before any case-specific extension/tab reload and record the inline results.
In Tools, run read_page on the active public target with {"filter":"all","include_text":true,"max_nodes":200}; record the returned ref and candidate text/role for the visible Example Domain heading.

In Tools, run find with {"query":"Example Domain","include_content":true,"limit":5}. Compare returned match refs against the current read_page candidate refs and check the matched candidate text/role is the visible heading.

Inspect used_cache and mode. A successful positive case requires a returned match whose ref is among current candidates and whose candidate text/role identifies the heading; a refusal, unavailable AI, missing match, or invented/unknown ref is not a pass.

For the separate reloaded run, reload the extension, close/reopen Tools, and reload the public tab. Run read_page again to reacquire the current heading candidate/ref, then repeat the same find query and candidate/ref/text check.
expected: For both warm and reloaded runs, find returns a match tied to a current read_page candidate ref whose candidate text/role identifies the visible Example Domain heading. Require the specific known match; any nonempty match list is insufficient.

If AI is unavailable/refuses, the expected result is an explicit unsuccessful/unverified run, not a pass. Do not assert an empty result for arbitrary no-match text: source sends zero-score candidates to AI, which can select one.
procedure_limits: AI-backed ranking can vary. The pass oracle is specifically a returned current candidate ref mapped to the visible known heading; record model refusal or a wrong/unknown ref as non-pass.

cases.title: Controlled manual execution: take_screenshot
preconditions: Before each case, obtain the resource permit required by docs/stabilization/PLAN.md and write a fresh receipt: source SHA and dirty-source hash if applicable, lockfile hash, output hash, WXT mode, extension runtime ID, Chrome version, profile label, auth/role/org state, permissions, backend identity, fixture IDs and timestamp. Use an already built, receipt-bound unpacked development artifact. Confirm loaded extension ID, source/output identity and build fingerprint. Wait for build completion before reload; reload the extension when required, reopen extension pages and the actual side panel/Tools tab, and reload controlled target tabs after extension reload. Treat service worker and offscreen contexts separately and verify each running build identity before acting. If either required context cannot be independently identified, leave that context/lifecycle dimension unverified and do not proceed as though its build identity is established. HMR alone is not acceptance evidence.

Run separately in genuine signed-in member and admin profiles. Tools is signed-in-only; guest applicability is not added by these proposals. Keep device organization and role visible in the receipt; do not infer one role's behavior from the other. Use only the owned public HTTPS fixtures described below.

Actual UI route: open the extension side panel, select Tools > Catalog, select All handlers, search and expand the exact handler, inspect its displayed local JSON schema, enter the specified JSON in Test runner and press Run. This route is source-confirmed in src/features/tools/ToolsView.tsx. It parses JSON and safe-parses local schemas, then calls handler.run directly with permissionMode=act and assignedTabId=null. It bypasses dispatcher permission/approval and role gates; these procedures do not establish dispatcher behavior, denied-permission behavior or live DB binding/advertisement.

Immediately before each Run, verify the selected active tab in the disposable test Chrome window is the owned public HTTPS fixture. Do not run in an everyday browsing profile. This source-only proposal covers warm direct-handler runs and the stated extension-reload observations only. Cold/idle service-worker restart with DevTools closed, controlled-page navigation, permission-denied recovery, and offline recovery are explicitly outside this proposal and remain unverified; do not count them as coverage or acceptance. Use the shared receipt and reload preamble. Target only the owned public page https://example.com/ and avoid any page containing personal, account or confidential information.
Set persist=false in every positive input so the procedure creates no cloud file or screenshot-index row. Do not use the Screenshots gallery button, which persists by design and is a different route.

Record activeTab declared/granted state from the existing extension permissions UI/build receipt. The manual runner bypasses dispatcher checks; if actual browser capture permission is unavailable, record the exact UI result and leave permission behavior unverified rather than labeling it dispatcher denial.

cases.title: Controlled manual execution: list_downloads
preconditions: Follow the complete resource permit and build/reload contract in docs/stabilization/PLAN.md. Use an existing receipt-bound development artifact; confirm its source SHA and tree hash match the loaded unpacked extension before opening the side panel. Record the exact artifact, Chrome version, disposable profile, role, permission state, and timestamp without recording credentials or personal browser data.

Use separate existing signed-in ordinary-member and admin test profiles. Keep each role's result separate. Guest applicability stays as currently recorded; these procedures do not test the Tools sign-in gate.

After the warm pass, repeat the applicable case after the source-relevant extension reload, side-panel reopen, and fixture-tab reload described in PLAN.md. A source-only procedure does not count as execution evidence.

In the signed-in side panel, open Tools → Catalog. For list_recent_history, list_downloads, and list_recently_closed, change the surface selector from its Agent surface default to All handlers, then search for the exact delegate name. For chrome_history and chrome_recently_closed, keep Agent surface and search for the exact canonical name. Expand the matching row, enter the listed JSON, select Run, and inspect the inline result. ToolsView runs local handlers directly and skips the dispatcher permission gate; these cases cover that user-initiated manual path only, not agent advertisement, Ask/Act gating, or dispatcher permission enforcement.

Use a dedicated disposable Chrome profile containing only synthetic/public test browsing data. Do not run these history/download/session reads in a personal profile or include unrelated returned records in evidence. Keep evidence limited to the known synthetic fixture and aggregate count where possible.

Before history procedures, visit two public pages in the disposable profile and record their exact URLs and visit time in the run receipt. If these controlled visits are absent from history, stop and leave the case unverified.

Before recently-closed procedures, verify the exact loaded Chrome artifact declares sessions in its required permissions and that the disposable profile has the permission; source declaration alone does not verify the loaded artifact. Then open a disposable tab to a public test page and close only that tab, preserving the fixture URL/title for comparison. There is no sessions Settings grant step: if the loaded permission or fixture is unavailable, stop and leave the relevant case unverified.

Use separate dedicated disposable Chrome profiles for member and admin. In each profile independently load the exact receipt-bound extension build, sign in as that role, prepare only that profile's controlled history and recently-closed fixtures, and perform the synthetic download in that profile before its download case. Record fixture URLs, tab session ID, downloaded filename and exact owned file path locally for that role; do not reuse a profile, fixture result, session ID, or download record across roles.

Run each proposed Catalog case separately as member and admin, including warm, malformed-schema and required reload steps against that role's own fixtures. Label evidence by role and loaded build receipt. Catalog output only proves direct local handler behavior when observed; it does not prove account authorization, dispatcher Ask/Act denial, or live advertised agent binding.

After each role's cases and sanitized evidence capture, close that role's Chrome profile. Remove and verify absence of only its recorded owned downloaded file, then retire/delete that role's disposable profile. Record either verified cleanup or explicitly unverified downloaded-file cleanup. Do not infer that deleting a profile removes a file Chrome saved elsewhere.
For this role, complete the shared receipt-bound setup in its own dedicated disposable Chrome profile and prepare this role's fixtures; repeat independently in a different profile for the other role.

Open committed owned fixture page tests/browser/fixtures/chrome-local-download.html in the dedicated disposable profile, click its Download synthetic fixture link, confirm completed filename matrx-owned-chrome-download-fixture.txt in Chrome Downloads, and record only that filename. This fixture source exists; completion remains unverified until a browser run.
Confirm the loaded Chrome artifact has the required downloads API permission, and select All handlers in Tools Catalog so the internal list_downloads delegate is visible.
steps: Warm run: open list_downloads and run with {"query":"<exact synthetic fixture filename>","state":"complete","limit":10}, substituting only the recorded fixture name.

Inspect the inline downloads array for the controlled fixture and compare filename, state, byte totals, and nonempty start_time with the known download. Avoid copying its URL or other download rows into the report.
Run with the same filename query and limit but omit state to confirm query matching still finds the fixture; compare by its synthetic filename only.

With the same Tools row selected, run {"query":"matrx-owned-chrome-download-fixture.txt","state":"paused","limit":10}; expect argument validation rejection before execution because state is limited to in_progress, interrupted, or complete.
After the required extension/panel reload, rerun the state-filtered query and confirm the same controlled record remains discoverable.

After this role's sanitized fixture assertion, close Chrome for this role; remove only its recorded owned downloaded file if one was created and verify absence, then retire/delete this role's disposable profile. If file path or absence cannot be confirmed, report downloaded-file cleanup unverified. Repeat the complete setup, fixture, run, and cleanup lifecycle independently for the other role. Preserve only sanitized build/run receipt and the specific assertion result.
expected: The response has count and downloads; the controlled fixture appears in the complete-state query with state complete, a matching filename, and coherent bytes_received/total_bytes.
The unfiltered query also finds the fixture. Results are requested newest first; the procedure does not require an exact total count.
If the controlled download fixture or required API is absent, stop and record the case unverified; never infer success from unrelated profile data.
The malformed-schema input is rejected by the runner and makes no Chrome API call; record the validation error without promoting any runtime status.
procedure_gaps: Direct Tools manual Run invokes the local handler without dispatcher authorization, so an authorization-denial / Ask-Act negative case is unreachable through this route. Separate dispatcher/agent coverage remains open.

Chrome sessions is a required manifest permission and these handlers only feature-detect API availability; there is no supported permission toggle in this procedure. Missing sessions in the exact loaded artifact is a preflight stop, not a permission-denial result.
This is source-derived procedure text only; all role results remain runtime-unverified until separately executed and reviewed.

Member and admin Catalog runs use separate disposable profiles and owned fixtures. Catalog observations do not establish account authorization, dispatcher Ask/Act denial, or live agent binding; those routes require separate unverified coverage.

Before native execution, freeze concrete per-role history/session fixture URLs and titles, visit/close steps, and resolve per-case versus per-role cleanup timing. Fresh review fa4ea18d leaves these design details open.

Remove and verify absence of only its recorded owned downloaded file, then retire/delete that role's disposable profile. Record either verified cleanup or explicitly unverified downloaded-file cleanup. Do not infer that deleting a profile removes a file Chrome saved elsewhere.
For this role, complete the shared receipt-bound setup in its own dedicated disposable Chrome profile and prepare this role's fixtures; repeat independently in a different profile for the other role.

cases.title: Controlled manual execution: webmcp_check_availability
preconditions: Run only after the owning runner approves inventory reconciliation and the resource permit. Record UTC time, Chrome version/channel, extension ID, source commit SHA, exact built artifact path plus SHA-256 and displayed version, profile identity, signed-in role, and the extension reload timestamp. Load that exact artifact in an owned disposable profile; confirm the side panel reports the same build identity. Repeat the build receipt after each full extension reload.

Use a secure-context page served from an origin you own (localhost is suitable), with a visible unique marker, a counter initialized to 0, and a read-only way to inspect both. In page DevTools, inspect the actual `document.modelContext` and method types. Do not polyfill or replace native objects. For documented local testing, use a Chrome build that actually exposes `chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing`, enable it and relaunch; record the actual channel/version and flag state. Chrome 149 is the documented Origin Trial start only, not a stated minimum for the local-flag route or a claim of general stable availability. Record the exact channel/build and flag state. If that flag or native API is absent, stop native-positive steps and mark them unresolved. If the actual native API is missing or incompatible, stop native-positive steps and record them unresolved; do not substitute a mock.

On owned secure-context localhost tab A, register one native page tool with a unique name and an object input schema requiring nonce:string. Its execute callback is a deterministic hold: set visible status to `entered:<nonce>` while keeping counter at 0; await a Promise resolved only by a `BroadcastChannel` message `{kind:'release',runId,nonce}`; after release increment A's counter exactly once and return `{nonce,counter:1,fixtureMarker:'webmcp-origin-A-<runId>'}`. Tab B is an owned same-origin control page with marker `webmcp-origin-B-<runId>`, counter 0, and two distinct real native fixture registrations `webmcp_fixture_B1_<runId>` and `webmcp_fixture_B2_<runId>` whose discovery metadata identifies B and whose callbacks are never invoked. B also has a Release A button that broadcasts the matching release and a Trigger A button for the extension-origin check below. Verify both B fixtures with its own actual `await document.modelContext.getTools()` call. After extension auto-registration settles on both tabs, snapshot both real catalogs; require B to have a different total count from A for the check oracle (register another uniquely named B fixture and resnapshot if necessary), with A-only and B-only fixture names for the list oracle. If counts later change or become equal, resnapshot and rerun; an equal-count check gives no A/B routing proof. This control channel coordinates the fixture; it does not replace, wrap, or monkeypatch any native WebMCP object. Await actual `document.modelContext.registerTool({name,description,inputSchema,execute})` and independently verify the real native `await document.modelContext.getTools()` contains the tool once. Record exact code, method types, and signatures. Implement Trigger A as a separate same-origin `BroadcastChannel` protocol: B's button sends `{kind:"trigger",runId,requestId,branch,toolName,input}` with fresh requestId after B is visibly active and records that state; A alone listens for the matching runId and unhandled requestId, verifies its A marker, sends `{kind:"accepted",runId,requestId,sourceMarker}` from A, then awaits its real `document.modelContext.getTools()`, finds the exact `matrx.<leaf>` or `matrx.chrome_webmcp` RegisteredTool by name, and calls `document.modelContext.executeTool(discoveredTool,input)`. A sends `{kind:"result",runId,requestId,sourceMarker,toolName,output}` or `{kind:"error",runId,requestId,sourceMarker,toolName,error}` when that Promise settles. B listens only for matching runId/requestId and A sourceMarker, records accepted plus final result/error, rejects duplicate or missing responses, and remains active through the native invocation. Use the documented object input for each branch; never create a fake RegisteredTool or call an extension bridge message directly. The `{kind:"release",runId,nonce}` message is a separate control used only after the action callback enters; it must not trigger a call or stand in for its result.

Use exact visible markers `webmcp-origin-A-<runId>` and `webmcp-origin-B-<runId>` and initialize both page counters to 0 for every run. Tab A's page tool is the only tool whose callback increments a counter. For manual Tools runs, focus the intended tab immediately before each run: ToolsView calls handler.run directly with assignedTabId:null and resolves whichever tab is focused. The held callback can prove the call's side effect/output stays on A after B is focused and releases it; it cannot prove when dispatcher target selection happened. Do not use that hold as evidence for read-only check/list, which never execute this callback. Manual runs do not prove dispatcher validation, admin gating, permissions, Ask/Act confirmation, or assigned-tab pinning.

For syntactically malformed text, use the Tools JSON editor and capture its `Invalid JSON` parser error before execution. For schema rejection, enter valid JSON with a wrong top-level type (for example `null`) and capture `Schema mismatch`; do not call either result a native API failure. For branch-level invalid values, use valid JSON that parses against the route schema and observe the handler's own structured result.

For the dispatcher lane, use a real agent invocation or real WebMCP page-to-extension call, record the exact authorized caller/role, loaded manifest/host access and Chrome scripting outcome, and capture the actual gate or confirmation UI. Check one read-tier branch and the action-tier call branch separately. An admin positive proves no negative role gate. External action calls require confirmation in both Ask and Act modes; decline once and verify no page side effect. Keep the feature-test procedure and inventory cell unexecuted until this run occurs. These handlers declare no `required_optional_permissions`; mark optional-permission dispatcher denial source-inapplicable, not a required negative. Preserve the permissions dimension by observing real admin denial, action confirmation, loaded `activeTab`/`scripting`/host access, and any actual restricted-tab `executeScript` rejection as distinct boundaries.

For the held page-tool call path, only use an exact tool that is actually advertised to the signed-in admin in the current request; if no live agent route exists, leave dispatcher tab-routing unresolved and retain the manual handler case. Start a real dispatcher action with Ask mode enabled while A is the assigned tab; wait until its actual approval card appears (handler has not run yet), focus B and confirm B is active, then approve. Require A status `entered:<nonce>` with counters still A=0/B=0; press B's Release A button; require returned fixtureMarker A, A counter=1, B counter=0. This forces focus to B before handler target resolution and release after entry. Also run a direct manual call from A, wait for entered, switch to B, release from B, and require the same A-only result, labeling it handler behavior only. For extension-origin routing, require real extension registrations on A. While B is already active, press B's Trigger A button for each branch and retain the runId/requestId accepted/result pair; A's own page script discovers the exact real `matrx.<leaf>` or `matrx.chrome_webmcp` RegisteredTool and invokes it through native `document.modelContext.executeTool(discoveredTool,input)`. For check, require the correlated A response to be `available:true` with `tool_count` equal to A's contemporaneous real catalog length and different from B's observed length; the check response contains no names. For list, require the correlated A response to include `webmcp_fixture_A_<runId>` and exclude both B fixture names, while B's independent native catalog shows both B fixtures and excludes A's; do not claim the fixture callback hold tested those read-only branches. For the action call, keep B active through the approval card, approve, then use B's Release A button and require the side effect only on A. For closed-origin checks, distinguish a request whose sender tab is already closed before delivery (`webmcp: origin tab unavailable`) from A closed after a real action approval is pending (explicit no-active-tab/closed-tab failure, no effect on B). Never infer a negative gate from an admin positive.

After page reload, the owned page script registers again and repeats native discovery/call with fresh runId, nonce, counters, and A/B markers. Fully reload the exact extension artifact, verify ID/version/path and a fresh build receipt, reload pages, and let the extension register again. For the audit receipt, ensure the disposable profile contains only owned fixture tabs across all windows and that the active browser window contains only A and B. On A, inspect the real catalog, find `matrx.list_open_tabs`, and execute the discovered RegisteredTool with `{all_windows:false,url:'http://localhost:<PORT>/webmcp-fixture/*'}` (the current handler schema supports both fields). Capture only the extension audit receipt fields `origin=webmcp`, call/tool identity, completion outcome, and timestamp; redact the returned tab array, URLs, titles, IDs, and query strings. Record the profile/tab hygiene check without retaining unrelated browsing data. Manual Tools runs are not WebMCP receipts. On owned secure-context localhost tab A, register one native page tool with a unique name and an object input schema requiring nonce:string. Its execute callback is a deterministic hold: set visible status to `entered:<nonce>` while keeping counter at 0; await a Promise resolved only by a `BroadcastChannel` message `{kind:'release',runId,nonce}`; after release increment A's counter exactly once and return `{nonce,counter:1,fixtureMarker:'webmcp-origin-A-<runId>'}`. Tab B is an owned same-origin control page with marker `webmcp-origin-B-<runId>`, counter 0, and two distinct real native fixture registrations `webmcp_fixture_B1_<runId>` and `webmcp_fixture_B2_<runId>` whose discovery metadata identifies B and whose callbacks are never invoked. B also has a Release A button that broadcasts the matching release and a Trigger A button for the extension-origin check below. Verify both B fixtures with its own actual `await document.modelContext.getTools()` call. After extension auto-registration settles on both tabs, snapshot both real catalogs; require B to have a different total count from A for the check oracle (register another uniquely named B fixture and resnapshot if necessary), with A-only and B-only fixture names for the list oracle. If counts later change or become equal, resnapshot and rerun; an equal-count check gives no A/B routing proof. This control channel coordinates the fixture; it does not replace, wrap, or monkeypatch any native WebMCP object. Await actual `document.modelContext.registerTool({name,description,inputSchema,execute})` and independently verify the real native `await document.modelContext.getTools()` contains the tool once. Record exact code, method types, and signatures. Implement Trigger A as a separate same-origin `BroadcastChannel` protocol: B's button sends `{kind:"trigger",runId,requestId,branch,toolName,input}` with fresh requestId after B is visibly active and records that state; A alone listens for the matching runId and unhandled requestId, verifies its A marker, sends `{kind:"accepted",runId,requestId,sourceMarker}` from A, then awaits its real `document.modelContext.getTools()`, finds the exact `matrx.<leaf>` or `matrx.chrome_webmcp` RegisteredTool by name, and calls `document.modelContext.executeTool(discoveredTool,input)`. A sends `{kind:"result",runId,requestId,sourceMarker,toolName,output}` or `{kind:"error",runId,requestId,sourceMarker,toolName,error}` when that Promise settles. B listens only for matching runId/requestId and A sourceMarker, records accepted plus final result/error, rejects duplicate or missing responses, and remains active through the native invocation. Use the documented object input for each branch; never create a fake RegisteredTool or call an extension bridge message directly. The `{kind:"release",runId,nonce}` message is a separate control used only after the action callback enters; it must not trigger a call or stand in for its result.

Use exact visible markers `webmcp-origin-A-<runId>` and `webmcp-origin-B-<runId>` and initialize both page counters to 0 for every run. Tab A's page tool is the only tool whose callback increments a counter. For manual Tools runs, focus the intended tab immediately before each run: ToolsView calls handler.run directly with assignedTabId:null and resolves whichever tab is focused. The held callback can prove the call's side effect/output stays on A after B is focused and releases it; it cannot prove when dispatcher target selection happened. Do not use that hold as evidence for read-only check/list, which never execute this callback. For syntactically malformed text, use the Tools JSON editor and capture its `Invalid JSON` parser error before execution. For schema rejection, enter valid JSON with a wrong top-level type (for example `null`) and capture `Schema mismatch`; do not call either result a native API failure. For branch-level invalid values, use valid JSON that parses against the route schema and observe the handler's own structured result.

Check one read-tier branch and the action-tier call branch separately. An admin positive proves no negative role gate. External action calls require confirmation in both Ask and Act modes; decline once and verify no page side effect. Keep the feature-test procedure and inventory cell unexecuted until this run occurs. These handlers declare no `required_optional_permissions`; mark optional-permission dispatcher denial source-inapplicable, not a required negative. For the held page-tool call path, only use an exact tool that is actually advertised to the signed-in admin in the current request; if no live agent route exists, leave dispatcher tab-routing unresolved and retain the manual handler case. Start a real dispatcher action with Ask mode enabled while A is the assigned tab; wait until its actual approval card appears (handler has not run yet), focus B and confirm B is active, then approve. Also run a direct manual call from A, wait for entered, switch to B, release from B, and require the same A-only result, labeling it handler behavior only. For extension-origin routing, require real extension registrations on A. Capture only the extension audit receipt fields `origin=webmcp`, call/tool identity, completion outcome, and timestamp; redact the returned tab array, URLs, titles, IDs, and query strings. Use the correlated B Trigger A protocol while B is active to invoke discovered `matrx.webmcp_list_page_tools` from A, then compare the returned A-only name with the independently observed B-only names; record requestId and source marker.

Run malformed JSON and valid wrong-top-level JSON validation checks. Run the dispatcher lane for read-tier/admin-only: verify the admin can invoke the advertised branch and a member is rejected by the real dispatcher before handler side effects. Check original-tab pinning across focus switch and explicit closed-origin behavior in the common preconditions.

Reload page and verify the page script re-registers once; rerun the list and compare to fresh `getTools()`. Fully reload the exact extension artifact, record a fresh receipt, reload page, re-register, and repeat. Capture real external `matrx.*` resource receipt and cleanup as specified above.

Schema/parser errors, unavailable native API, scripting failures, admin denial, and closed origin are distinct outcomes; preserve each exact result and its evidence. Admin success does not prove member denial. Read-only list routing is established only by a real native page-origin invocation emitted from A while B is active and a response matching A's distinct catalog; the held fixture callback is irrelevant to this branch.
Manual Tools execution establishes only direct handler behavior. Current source does not claim that inventory metadata alone proves the handler is advertised to an agent.

cases.title: Controlled manual execution: get_guidance_item
preconditions: Use the resource permit and build-receipt procedure in docs/stabilization/PLAN.md. Match the receipt-bound development artifact, source SHA/tree hash, loaded unpacked extension identity, WXT mode, required storage permission, and Chrome version. Record the receipt, role/profile, and timestamp without credentials or unrelated storage contents.

Use existing signed-in member and admin dedicated test profiles separately. Do not create or change accounts, roles, organizations, or permissions. Confirm an active organization is selected on each device because cloud writes require it. Guest remains inapplicable to the signed-in Tools UI.
For each profile, perform the warm pass, reload the same extension and reopen the side panel, then perform the specified post-reload checks. If the artifact changes, obtain a matching new receipt.

In the signed-in side panel open Tools → Catalog, leave the selector at Agent surface, search the exact tool name, expand its row, replace the test-runner JSON, select Run, and inspect the inline result. The guidance tools are in CANONICAL_SURFACE.

The runner validates JSON against the handler schema and invokes the local handler directly with conversationId=null and assignedTabId=null. It bypasses dispatcher authorization. This procedure covers the manual handler path; agent advertisement, Ask/Act gating, and guest denial require separate cases.

In each role/profile, use save_guidance_note through the same manual Tools runner with a unique recognizable domain (for example procedure-guidance.invalid), caption (for example EXT-F-4139-T01 member fixture), and short harmless text (for example owned synthetic guidance note). These are test-created items, never pre-existing user data.

Require save_guidance_note to return {ok:true,id:<UUID>,domain:<chosen domain>}. Record the exact returned UUID privately for subsequent get/delete calls; use no guessed ID for a positive branch. Keep separate IDs for member and admin. Stop that profile if saving fails.

Keep only the returned IDs and sanitized result evidence. Do not browse, copy, modify, or delete unrelated guidance. After every attempt, clean up each successfully created fixture by its exact returned ID; if cleanup cannot be confirmed locally and by an exact-ID cloud tombstone or exact-ID absence when the save never reached cloud, record an open cleanup item for that ID and do not claim a full pass.

Saving and deleting update chrome.storage.local first and start fire-and-forget cloud work. A local {ok:true}, a warm read, or extension reload alone does not prove cloud persistence, sync, or durable deletion.

For any cloud claim, verify only the exact owned UUID in extend.wbx_guidance using an authorized scoped read or observe an equivalent independent hydration in a separate profile signed in as the same principal. After save, require the matching live row and fields; after delete, require a deleted_at tombstone for a confirmed cloud row and no live item after independent hydration under the same principal. If the save never reached cloud, exact-ID cloud absence is sufficient for cleanup but does not verify cloud deletion. Do not use a broad table dump or inspect unrelated rows. If that observation is unavailable, report cloud sync/deletion unverified while retaining the local handler result.

Cloud hydration runs on signed-in sidepanel mount and merges last-write-wins; a same-profile reload usually retains the local cache and is only a local persistence check. A failed fire-and-forget push or tombstone can leave a cloud mismatch or permit reappearance; record this as a failure or unresolved cloud limit, not a pass.
Complete shared build/profile setup and create an owned synthetic note in the current profile through save_guidance_note; retain its exact returned UUID.
Run the full sequence independently in the existing member and admin profiles. Guest remains inapplicable to Tools UI.

For cloud evidence record the same signed-in principal and authorized organization/access context in both profiles. Confirm an explicitly selected organization for each save; do not copy account or extension storage between role profiles.

Run EXT-F-4140-T01 on the owned UUID in the same profile to clean it up. If the delete case cannot run, delete only that exact fixture through the same manual tool and verify get returns missing. Repeat all steps with a separately created admin/member fixture.
