preconditions: https://www.selenium.dev/selenium/web/web-form.html is Selenium's public Web form demo. Its observed page lists a text input, default checkbox, select, and submit button. Never enter a credential, choose a file, or submit the form. Before execution verify the live page still presents the named controls; if it has changed, stop and keep the case unverified.

Admit the appropriate resource permit. In separate member and admin profiles load the exact candidate development extension, record source commit, lockfile hash, build receipt, extension ID/version/Loaded from path in chrome://extensions, Chrome version, and signed-in role. Tools is sign-in gated; guest has no manual Tools case. Do not infer member dispatcher access from a direct manual run.

Open only a disposable public-demo tab. In Tools > Catalog choose All handlers; run list_open_tabs with {} and record the one tab ID whose full URL matches the demo. Keep that tab selected when running CDP input; canonical form_input and navigate require the same ID as a decimal string. Do not use an unrelated or authenticated tab.

Search each exact name, open its row, verify the displayed input schema and tier, enter the complete JSON, click Run, and inspect the inline output/error plus the real page. The manual runner validates Zod then calls handler.run with permissionMode=act and assignedTabId=null; it bypasses dispatcher approval and cannot establish the agent's assigned-tab or role/permission enforcement.

Warm: where all case-specific preconditions are met, execute positive and negative segments after loading the candidate extension without a preceding full extension Reload; record result, visible page state, tab ID, and immediate debugger banner/attachment delta.

Post-reload: where all case-specific preconditions are met, use chrome://extensions Reload for that exact extension, confirm the same extension ID/version/path, reopen Tools, refresh the disposable demo page, reacquire its tab ID and any read_page ref/bounds, then repeat the same segments. A web-page refresh or side-panel reopen alone is insufficient.

All four inventory permissions dimensions remain unresolved. The two CDP input handlers declare privileged tier and debugger; debugger is a base manifest permission with no Settings revoke switch. The direct Tools Run path skips requestConfirmation and optional-permission checks. A future separately mapped Chat/Pilot dispatcher denial needs the exact tool advertised to the tested role, a known owned tab, Ask mode for action tools or the mandatory privileged card for CDP, the tester choosing Deny in the actual approval UI, and an unchanged-page oracle. No such live route or refusal was established by this source-only proposal. Malformed JSON, stale refs and invalid tab IDs are not permission tests.

Admin only: record cdp_attached_tabs baseline and the owned debugger banner, then record the owned attachment/banner immediately after each positive CDP run. If still attached, use cdp_detach for exactly the owned ID and confirm disappearance. If it has already idle-detached or a worker restart swept it, record that state without claiming explicit cleanup; cdp_attached_tabs is only the current worker's in-memory set. Member: do not use admin-only helpers through the manual gate bypass; close only the disposable demo tab and confirm its banner clears. Preserve pre-existing attachments and unrelated tabs.
signed-in member/admin, decimal string tab ID and public demo Text input visibly present. The page is not a credential or submission fixture.
Run read_page with {"tab_id":"$TAB_ID"} and identify one fresh ref for the visible non-password Text input; do not guess a ref or reuse it after navigation/read_page reassigns attributes.
steps: Tools > Catalog > All handlers > form_input. Run {"tab_id":"$TAB_ID","ref":"$TEXT_REF","value":"matrx-4151"} using the exact fresh ref and decimal string tab ID.

Inspect the real Text input and run read_page to verify value matrx-4151. This read_page removes/reassigns all data-matrx-ref attributes, so save the NEW ref it now reports for the same Text input as $REF_BEFORE_REFRESH. Do not click Submit or enter secrets.

Refresh the web page normally; before any new read_page, run {"tab_id":"$TAB_ID","ref":"$REF_BEFORE_REFRESH","value":"matrx-stale"}. Require {"ok":false,"reason":"No element for $REF_BEFORE_REFRESH"} and unchanged input. This isolates page-refresh invalidation from the earlier read_page reassignment. Separately use {"tab_id":"not-id","ref":"$REF_BEFORE_REFRESH","value":"matrx-4151"} for explicit invalid-tab refusal.
Repeat warm and post-reload phases; reacquire a fresh ref after every page refresh and extension Reload.
expected: Positive returns {"ok":true,"tag":"input"} and the exact field visibly contains matrx-4151. activateTab can switch browser focus; compare the same owned tab ID before/after.

The ref saved from the last read_page before page refresh returns No element for that ref after refresh, with no intervening read_page; the refreshed field stays unchanged. Invalid tab ID returns {"ok":false,"reason":"Invalid tab_id: not-id"}. Neither is an approval-denial test.
The form remains unsubmitted and no unrelated tab is changed.

cases.title: Controlled manual execution: chrome_webmcp
preconditions: Run only after the owning runner approves inventory reconciliation and the resource permit. Record UTC time, Chrome version/channel, extension ID, source commit SHA, exact built artifact path plus SHA-256 and displayed version, profile identity, signed-in role, and the extension reload timestamp. Load that exact artifact in an owned disposable profile; confirm the side panel reports the same build identity. Repeat the build receipt after each full extension reload.

Use a secure-context page served from an origin you own (localhost is suitable), with a visible unique marker, a counter initialized to 0, and a read-only way to inspect both. In page DevTools, inspect the actual `document.modelContext` and method types. Do not polyfill or replace native objects. For documented local testing, use a Chrome build that actually exposes `chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing`, enable it and relaunch; record the actual channel/version and flag state. Chrome 149 is the documented Origin Trial start only, not a stated minimum for the local-flag route or a claim of general stable availability. Record the exact channel/build and flag state. If that flag or native API is absent, stop native-positive steps and mark them unresolved. If the actual native API is missing or incompatible, stop native-positive steps and record them unresolved; do not substitute a mock.

On owned secure-context localhost tab A, register one native page tool with a unique name and an object input schema requiring nonce:string. Its execute callback is a deterministic hold: set visible status to `entered:<nonce>` while keeping counter at 0; await a Promise resolved only by a `BroadcastChannel` message `{kind:'release',runId,nonce}`; after release increment A's counter exactly once and return `{nonce,counter:1,fixtureMarker:'webmcp-origin-A-<runId>'}`. Tab B is an owned same-origin control page with marker `webmcp-origin-B-<runId>`, counter 0, and two distinct real native fixture registrations `webmcp_fixture_B1_<runId>` and `webmcp_fixture_B2_<runId>` whose discovery metadata identifies B and whose callbacks are never invoked. B also has a Release A button that broadcasts the matching release and a Trigger A button for the extension-origin check below. Verify both B fixtures with its own actual `await document.modelContext.getTools()` call. After extension auto-registration settles on both tabs, snapshot both real catalogs; require B to have a different total count from A for the check oracle (register another uniquely named B fixture and resnapshot if necessary), with A-only and B-only fixture names for the list oracle. If counts later change or become equal, resnapshot and rerun; an equal-count check gives no A/B routing proof. This control channel coordinates the fixture; it does not replace, wrap, or monkeypatch any native WebMCP object. Await actual `document.modelContext.registerTool({name,description,inputSchema,execute})` and independently verify the real native `await document.modelContext.getTools()` contains the tool once. Record exact code, method types, and signatures. Implement Trigger A as a separate same-origin `BroadcastChannel` protocol: B's button sends `{kind:"trigger",runId,requestId,branch,toolName,input}` with fresh requestId after B is visibly active and records that state; A alone listens for the matching runId and unhandled requestId, verifies its A marker, sends `{kind:"accepted",runId,requestId,sourceMarker}` from A, then awaits its real `document.modelContext.getTools()`, finds the exact `matrx.<leaf>` or `matrx.chrome_webmcp` RegisteredTool by name, and calls `document.modelContext.executeTool(discoveredTool,input)`. A sends `{kind:"result",runId,requestId,sourceMarker,toolName,output}` or `{kind:"error",runId,requestId,sourceMarker,toolName,error}` when that Promise settles. B listens only for matching runId/requestId and A sourceMarker, records accepted plus final result/error, rejects duplicate or missing responses, and remains active through the native invocation. Use the documented object input for each branch; never create a fake RegisteredTool or call an extension bridge message directly. The `{kind:"release",runId,nonce}` message is a separate control used only after the action callback enters; it must not trigger a call or stand in for its result.

Use exact visible markers `webmcp-origin-A-<runId>` and `webmcp-origin-B-<runId>` and initialize both page counters to 0 for every run. Tab A's page tool is the only tool whose callback increments a counter. For manual Tools runs, focus the intended tab immediately before each run: ToolsView calls handler.run directly with assignedTabId:null and resolves whichever tab is focused. The held callback can prove the call's side effect/output stays on A after B is focused and releases it; it cannot prove when dispatcher target selection happened. Do not use that hold as evidence for read-only check/list, which never execute this callback. Manual runs do not prove dispatcher validation, admin gating, permissions, Ask/Act confirmation, or assigned-tab pinning.

For syntactically malformed text, use the Tools JSON editor and capture its `Invalid JSON` parser error before execution. For schema rejection, enter valid JSON with a wrong top-level type (for example `null`) and capture `Schema mismatch`; do not call either result a native API failure. For branch-level invalid values, use valid JSON that parses against the route schema and observe the handler's own structured result.

For the dispatcher lane, use a real agent invocation or real WebMCP page-to-extension call, record the exact authorized caller/role, loaded manifest/host access and Chrome scripting outcome, and capture the actual gate or confirmation UI. Check one read-tier branch and the action-tier call branch separately. An admin positive proves no negative role gate. External action calls require confirmation in both Ask and Act modes; decline once and verify no page side effect. Keep the feature-test procedure and inventory cell unexecuted until this run occurs. These handlers declare no `required_optional_permissions`; mark optional-permission dispatcher denial source-inapplicable, not a required negative. Preserve the permissions dimension by observing real admin denial, action confirmation, loaded `activeTab`/`scripting`/host access, and any actual restricted-tab `executeScript` rejection as distinct boundaries.

For the held page-tool call path, only use an exact tool that is actually advertised to the signed-in admin in the current request; if no live agent route exists, leave dispatcher tab-routing unresolved and retain the manual handler case. Start a real dispatcher action with Ask mode enabled while A is the assigned tab; wait until its actual approval card appears (handler has not run yet), focus B and confirm B is active, then approve. Require A status `entered:<nonce>` with counters still A=0/B=0; press B's Release A button; require returned fixtureMarker A, A counter=1, B counter=0. This forces focus to B before handler target resolution and release after entry. Also run a direct manual call from A, wait for entered, switch to B, release from B, and require the same A-only result, labeling it handler behavior only. For extension-origin routing, require real extension registrations on A. While B is already active, press B's Trigger A button for each branch and retain the runId/requestId accepted/result pair; A's own page script discovers the exact real `matrx.<leaf>` or `matrx.chrome_webmcp` RegisteredTool and invokes it through native `document.modelContext.executeTool(discoveredTool,input)`. For check, require the correlated A response to be `available:true` with `tool_count` equal to A's contemporaneous real catalog length and different from B's observed length; the check response contains no names. For list, require the correlated A response to include `webmcp_fixture_A_<runId>` and exclude both B fixture names, while B's independent native catalog shows both B fixtures and excludes A's; do not claim the fixture callback hold tested those read-only branches. For the action call, keep B active through the approval card, approve, then use B's Release A button and require the side effect only on A. For closed-origin checks, distinguish a request whose sender tab is already closed before delivery (`webmcp: origin tab unavailable`) from A closed after a real action approval is pending (explicit no-active-tab/closed-tab failure, no effect on B). Never infer a negative gate from an admin positive.

After page reload, the owned page script registers again and repeats native discovery/call with fresh runId, nonce, counters, and A/B markers. Fully reload the exact extension artifact, verify ID/version/path and a fresh build receipt, reload pages, and let the extension register again. For the audit receipt, ensure the disposable profile contains only owned fixture tabs across all windows and that the active browser window contains only A and B. On A, inspect the real catalog, find `matrx.list_open_tabs`, and execute the discovered RegisteredTool with `{all_windows:false,url:'http://localhost:<PORT>/webmcp-fixture/*'}` (the current handler schema supports both fields). Capture only the extension audit receipt fields `origin=webmcp`, call/tool identity, completion outcome, and timestamp; redact the returned tab array, URLs, titles, IDs, and query strings. Record the profile/tab hygiene check without retaining unrelated browsing data. Manual Tools runs are not WebMCP receipts. Cleanup by unregistering only if the native API supports it; otherwise close the owned profile/pages and verify no fixture tab or owned registration remains.
steps: On focused tab A, run `{"action":"check"}`. Compare its delegated result to a direct run of `webmcp_check_availability` and to the awaited native catalog count. Then run `{"action":"list"}` and compare the delegated list to direct `webmcp_list_page_tools` and the native RegisteredTool fixture. Record each branch separately for C02 and C03.

Run `{"action":"call","tool_name":"<unique fixture name>","arguments":{"nonce":"<fresh nonce>"}}`; require returned nonce/marker and exactly one independent counter increment. Record as C04. Verify tab B remains unchanged.

Run a syntactically valid unknown action (for example `{"action":"bad"}`) through Tools and capture schema mismatch before handler execution. Run call without tool_name and with unknown tool name; require their distinct bounded handler errors and no counter change. Separately run malformed JSON and valid JSON `null` to distinguish form parser from schema validation.

Run check/list against an actual API-absent context only if direct page observation proves absence; otherwise mark that branch unverified. Record restricted-tab scripting failure separately. In the real dispatcher lane, check admin success and member denial separately, read-tier confirmation policy for check/list, action-tier confirmation for call in Ask and Act, denial with unchanged counter, and approval with one increment. Neither canonical nor leaf handler declares `required_optional_permissions`; catalog activeTab/scripting metadata does not create an optional-permission dispatcher denial. Record loaded manifest activeTab/scripting, host access, actual Chrome executeScript rejection where reproducible, admin denial, and confirmation separately.

Exercise the common precondition's held A action with B focused, extension-origin invocation from A while B is already active, and separate closed-origin timings. Do not use the callback hold to claim read-only check/list targeting. The canonical tool's `tierFor` makes check/list read-tier and call action-tier; verify the observed controls match. Then page reload and full exact-artifact extension reload, fresh build receipts, native re-registration, all three branch repeats, external resource receipt and cleanup. For B-triggered A check/list/call, discover `matrx.chrome_webmcp` in A's real catalog and invoke it through the runId/requestId protocol with `{action:"check"}`, `{action:"list"}`, or `{action:"call",tool_name:"webmcp_fixture_A_<runId>",arguments:{nonce:"<fresh nonce>"}}`; retain each correlated output. Check must match A's unequal real count, list must show A-only fixture names, and call must return A marker with A=1/B=0 after a separate release.
expected: Each canonical branch must delegate to its corresponding current leaf and agree with its leaf result. Positive call requires actual native discovery, execution output and independent counter readback. The held call must show entered on A before release, B active at release, then A=1/B=0; check/list routing uses separate B-triggered A invocation without claiming a callback hold. For check, compare count to A and B contemporaneous native catalog lengths, requiring them unequal; only list can compare fixture names.

Invalid action is rejected by the outer route schema; missing tool_name is a handler-level error after route parsing; unknown page tool is a leaf execution result. Malformed JSON and wrong top-level JSON are UI parser/schema failures, respectively.

Admin positive does not prove member denial. A manual Tools run does not establish dispatcher permission enforcement, runtime permission state, assigned-tab behavior or confirmation. Capture actual UI and no-side-effect evidence for every denied call.

The 2026-10-04 census records canonical DB metadata active and exact-name leaf metadata absent. It does not establish current advertisement of leaves, role visibility, or callability; verify live request/dispatcher evidence rather than claiming it from the census.
